title: Single-cell RNA transcriptomics in mice reveals embryonic origin of fibrosis due to maternal obesity

sections.abstract:
Over 40% of pregnant women in the USA are obese which negatively affects fetal development and offspring health. Maternal obesity (MO) leads to fibrotic infiltration in multiple tissues and organs of offspring during their adulthood although the origin and mechanisms are unclear.

C57BL/6J female mice were fed a control and high-fat diet to mimic MO condition. Embryonic somatic tissues were obtained at E9.5, E11.5, and E13.5 (equivalent to 6 weeks of human pregnancy) from control (CON) and MO mice for single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq). To explore the role of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), AMPK was activated by metformin and A769662, and knocked out in embryonic mesenchymal cells (EMC) using AMPKα1 floxed mice.

Using unsupervised clustering, we identified three major cell populations with fibrogenic capacity. Compared to CON, the population of fibrogenic cells increased dramatically (by ∼125%) due to MO, supporting an embryonic origin of fibrosis in the offspring. MO induced inflammatory response and elevated expression of transforming growth factor β (TGFβ) signalling and fibrogenic genes in embryos. MO inhibited AMPK and its activation by metformin and A769662 inhibited TGFβ signalling and fibrogenesis.

MO profoundly enhances embryonic fibrogenesis, explaining the origin of fibrosis in the offspring of mothers living with obesity. Our data underscore the importance of early intervention, before 5–6 weeks of pregnancy, in improving embryonic development, and AMPK is an amiable target for suppressing excessive fibrogenesis in MO embryos to assist increasing populations of obese mothers having healthy children.

This work was funded by National Institutes of Health Grant R01HD067449.

Keywords: Maternal obesity, scRNA-seq, TGFβ, PRRX1, AMPK, Embryo, Fibrogenesis
sections.introduction:
In the United States, around 42.1% of reproductive aged women are living with obesity. 1 Maternal obesity (MO) not only causes complications for the mothers, but also impedes fetal development, leading to increased susceptibility to diabetes, hypertension, overweight, and cardiovascular illnesses in offspring at adulthood. 2 , 3 We previously found that MO leads to fibrotic and fatty infiltration in skeletal muscle of offspring, which is typically only observed in elders. 4 , 5 , 6 , 7 During ageing or muscular dystrophy, progressive muscle fiber loss occurs, replaced by increased fibrotic and fatty tissues, impairing skeletal muscle contractile force and leading to frailty. 8 Besides skeletal muscle, we observed that MO enhances fibrogenesis in brown adipose tissue 9 and cardiac muscle. 5 , 10 , 11 In addition, multiple laboratories reported hepatic fibrosis in offspring due to MO, 12 , 13 , 14 and also in the kidney. 15 However, mechanisms leading to fibrosis in multiple tissues and organs in offspring by MO remain to be defined, which represents a critical knowledge gap since fibrosis is a leading cause of functional deterioration during aging and under pathophysiological conditions. 13 , 16 Because embryonic fibrogenic cells are the source of fibrogenic cells in offspring, we hypothesized that fibrosis in MO offspring is due to enhanced fibrogenesis during embryonic development. Using single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq), we observed a stunning elevation of fibrogenesis in the early embryos due to MO, providing an explanation for the fibrosis in offspring.

Maternal obesity induces a low-grade inflammatory condition in placenta and fetuses indicated by the upregulation of pro-inflammatory cytokines including interlukin-6 (IL-6), IL-1β, and tumour necrosis factor-α (TNFα), and activation of NF-kB signalling pathway. 17 , 18 Inflammation is known to activate transforming growth factor-β (TGFβ) and pathological fibrogenesis, 19 partially via the activation of Paired related homeobox 1 (PRRX1). 20 , 21

AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) is a master regulator of metabolism. 22 AMPK has three subunits (α, β and γ); there are two isoforms for the catalytic α subunits (α1 and α2) with the α1 subunit being prevalent and widely expressed. 23 During energy deficiency and/or metabolic stress, AMPK is activated to restore energy homeostasis. 24 AMPK activation activates Sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator-1α (PGC1α) to improve oxidative metabolism. AMPK suppresses NF-kB signalling and inflammation and the subsequent TGFβ signalling. 23 , 25 Thus, AMPK is a common drug target for diabetes, insulin resistance, and other metabolic diseases. However, AMPK is inhibited in fetal tissues due to MO. 26 , 27 , 28 We further hypothesized that MO promotes embryonic fibrogenesis by inhibition of AMPK, which activates the TGFβ/PRRX1 pathway. Consistently, we found that AMPK activation by metformin inhibits inflammation and embryonic fibrosis, suggesting that AMPK is an effective therapeutic target to ameliorate pathogenic fibrogenesis in MO embryos.
sections.methods:
Wild-type C57BL/6J female mice were purchased from The Jackson Laboratory (Bar Harbor, ME, USA). To induce obesity, female mice were randomly assigned to two groups at 8 weeks of age and provided ad libitum access to either a control diet (containing 10% of energy from fat; D12450H, Research Diets, New Brunswick, NJ, USA, CON group) or a high-fat diet (containing 45% of energy from fat; D12451, Research Diets, MO group) for 10 weeks, and then mated with randomly selected males maintained on a regular diet. 29 In the early morning, mating was confirmed by the presence of vaginal plug and designated as day E0.5. The respective diets for each group were maintained during pregnancy. At E9.5, E11.5, and E13.5, mice were euthanized, and embryos were collected. All animals were euthanized by CO 2 inhalation and cervical dislocation before the collection of embryos following AVMA Guidelines for the Euthanasia of Animals (2020), approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) of Washington State University (WSU). All animal studies were conducted in the Association for Assessment and Accreditation of Laboratory Animal Care (AAALAC) accredited animal facility at the WSU and approved by IACUC protocol number: 6704.

To visualize the distribution of PDGFR α + cells, a marker of embryonic fibroblasts, we crossed the CON and MO female mice with PDGFRα EGFP (Strain #:007669, Jackson Lab) male mice which express eGFP under the Pdgfra promoter. We collected the embryo at E13.5 and embedded with O.C.T compound (Tissue-Tek, Sakura Finetek USA) and sectioned for fluorescence imaging. In addition, in vivo fluorescence imaging and relative GFP expression of CT and MO embryos were measured by using IVIS Spectrum In Vivo Imaging System (PerkinElmer, USA).

Mice were fasted for 6 h with water access ad libitum . d -glucose was injected intraperitoneally into mice at 2 g/kg of body weight, respectively. Serum was obtained at 0, 15, 30, 60, and 120 min after administration from the tail vein and glucose was analysed by an automatic glucose monitor (Contour, Bayer, IN, United States) as previously described. 30

To ensure embryos of similar developmental stages, Theiler Stage 15, 19 and 21 with somite number 23–26, 45–47 and 52–55 respectively were confirmed for the embryos at E9.5, E11.5 and E13.5 days. 31 Embryos were collected after removing the head and first 7 somite pairs under a dissecting microscope (Leica DFC450C). 29 , 32 For each time point, 15 embryos from 3 pregnancies were collected from each of MO and CON groups respectively and pooled together for preparation of cell suspension. Embryos were minced and incubated at 37 °C for 15 min with TryLE Express dissociation reagent (Gibco; Cat# 12605.010). The dissociated cells were filtered with a 40 μM cell strainer and libraries were constructed according to 10× Genomics protocol by using Chromium Single Cell 3’ Library & Gel Bead Kit v3 and sequenced in an Illumina NovaSeq 600S4 as previously described. 29

Cell Ranger v 7.0 (10× Genomics) was used for preprocessing raw sequences and mapped to the mouse mm10 transcriptome. All libraries from 3 different time points were merged together by using “merge” function of Seurat v 4.3.0 in R. 33 All cells possessing UMIs >200,000 and < 500 genes were removed and cells with >20% mitochondrial gene were excluded before further analysis to filter low quality cells and remove doublets. A total of 75,402 cells were retained for downstream analysis. A global-scaling normalization method “LogNormalize” with default feature was used to normalize the resulting dataset. Dataset was scaled and Principal component analysis (PCA) was performed to reduce the linear dimensionality. Elbow plot was produced to rank the PCAs and 35 PCAs were selected to cluster cells. Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) was run for non-linear dimensionality and clusters were embedded in Dimplot. Markers from the defined clusters were identified by using “FindAllMarkers” function of Seurat. Differential gene expression between MO and CON groups was calculated by using the “FindMarkers” function of Wilcox test.

Trajectory inference and pseudotime analysis were performed using R package Monocle 3. 34 Briefly, three identified fibrogenic clusters were imported in Monocole by using “cell_data_set” function. Cells were then re-clustered in Monocole by “Cluster_cells” function and trajectory graph were prepared by “learn_graph”. Changes in the expression of genes with progression of pseudotime were measured by “plot_genes_in_pseudotime” after ordering them according to their progress through developmental stages by calling “order_cellsR”.

For gene ontology (GO) analysis, we used ShinyGO 77.0. The significantly upregulated and downregulated DEGs from MO group were used as input for ShinyGO and KEGG pathway database to reveal the enriched pathways impacted due to MO. Significantly enriched pathways (Enrichment FDR >0) were selected and used for creating plot. For Gene Set Enrichment analysis, Fast Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (fgsea) V1.28 was used. The DEGs from MO group and their “Fold Change” were used as input in fgesa and their enrichment score was calculated.

To infer cell to cell communication among the cell clusters obtained from Seurat, we used CellChat V2 (R package). Seurat object and CellChatDB of mouse were used to create cellChat object. Next, the differential cell–cell communication pathways were calculated by comparing two groups where genes expressed by <10% of cells in Seurat clusters were removed and P < 0.05 was set as a cut off value.

Differential gene expressions between two groups across all clusters were calculated by using pseudo-bulk single cell aggregation approach with edgeR. We used “Seurat2PB” function to aggregate all reads together and prepared the pseudo-bulk sample. After normalization of the aggregated data, we used quantile-adjusted conditional maximum likelihood (qCML) method to calculate the DEGs between CON and MO groups with a cutoff value of P < 0.05.

Embryonic mesenchymal cells (EMCs) were isolated from control (CON, AMPKα1 fl/fl , Stock No. 014141, Jackson Lab) without Cre/ER and AMPK KO (AMPKα1 fl/fl with Cre/ER, Stock No. 008463, Jackson Lab) embryos at E13.5 as previously described. 35 Briefly, after removing the head, limbs, and internal organs, the remaining somatic tissues were rinsed by PBS and minced. Tissues were incubated in a shaking incubator at 37 °C with 0.025% trypsin/ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) (Invitrogen, CA) and filtered through 40 μM strainer. After centrifuging the cells at 400× g for 5 min, the residual cell pellet was gently suspended in DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin-streptomycin.

C3H/10T1/2 (CCL-226, ATCC, RRID: CVCL_0190) and isolated EMCs were incubated with growth medium composed of DMEM with 10% FBS (Gibco # 10.439.001) and 1% penicillin-streptomycin (Sigma, #P0781). 36 When reached 80% confluency, growth medium was supplemented with or without TGFβ (10 ng/ml; Peprotech, USA, Cat# 110-21C) for 48 h to initiate fibrogenesis. In addition, to pharmacologically activate AMPK, 500 μM MET (Metformin; MP Biomedicals, Cat# 151691) and 50 μM A76 (A769662; TOCRIS, Cat# 3336) was supplemented as described previously. 23 When EMCs reached 80% of confluence, 4-hydroxytamoxifen (Sigma–Aldrich; Cat# 5.08225.001) was added and incubated for 48 h to knockout AMPKα1 and followed by incubation with/without TGFβ (10 ng/ml) for 24 h. The cells were harvested for further analyses. Related information regarding cell line validation is mentioned in Reagent Validation File.

AMPKα1 fl/fl Female mice (Stock No: 014141, Jackson Lab, Bar Harbor, Maine) were crossed with R26-Cre Male mice (Stock No: 004847, Jackson Lab, Bar Harbor, Maine) to produce AMPKα1 fl/fl− CreER embryos. Cre expression was induced by tamoxifen (Sigma–Aldrich; CAS# 10540-29-1) injection (75 mg/kg body weight intraperitoneally at E9.5 and E11.5 to knock out AMPK from AMPKα1 fl/fl− CreER embryos (AMPK-KO), while AMPKα1 fl/fl embryos injected with tamoxifen at E9.5 and E11.5 were used as the control group (AMPK-WT). Mice were euthanized in accordance with the aforementioned protocol, and the embryos were collected at E 13.5 for subsequent analysis.

In the metformin administration study, female C57BL/6J mice were randomly assigned to three groups at 8 weeks of age and provided ad libitum access to either a control diet (containing 10% of energy from fat; D12450H, Research Diets, New Brunswick, NJ, USA, CON group) or two high-fat diet (containing 45% of energy from fat; D12451, Research Diets, MO and MO-MET group) for 10 weeks. One week before mating, metformin (MP Biomedicals, Cat# 151691) was administered to obese female mice of MO-MET group via drinking water (0.5%) and continued during pregnancy. Embryos were collected at E 13.5 for further analysis after euthanizing the mice following the protocol mentioned above.

Total RNA was isolated from tissues and cells using the TRIzol reagent (Invitrogen, Cat# 15596018) according to the manufacturer's instructions. The iScript cDNA Synthesis Kit (Bio-Rad, Cat# 1708891) was used for reverse transcription to synthesis cDNA. The SsoAdvanced Universal SYBR Green Supermix (Bio-Rad, Cat# 172570) was used to assess the relative mRNA expression using real-time quantitative PCR (iQ5, Bio-Rad), and RNA expression was calculated to that of 18S ribosomal RNA. All primer sequences used in this study are listed in the Supplementary Table S9 .

Proteins were isolated from cells or tissues by using lysis buffer, separated by using SDS-PAGE on 10% polyacrylamide gels and transferred to a nitrocellulose membrane. The following primary antibodies were used to probe the membrane: AMPKα (Cell Signaling Technology Cat# 2532, RRID: AB_330331 ), Phospho-AMPKα (Cell Signaling Tech. Cat# 4185, RRID: AB_2169402 ), SMAD3 (Cell Signaling Tech. Cat# 9523, RRID: AB_2193182 ), Phospho-SMAD3 (Cell Signaling Tech. Cat# 9520, RRID: AB_2193207 ), NF-κB p65 (Cell Signaling Tech. Cat# 3987, RRID: AB_2341215 ), Phospho-NF-κB p65 (Cell Signaling Tech. Cat# 3037, RRID: AB_2341216 ), PRRX1 (MyBioSource.com.; Cat# MBS9605728), Pdgfrα (Cell Signaling Tech. Cat# 3164, RRID: AB_2162351 ), COL1A1 (Cell Signaling Tech. Cat# 72026, RRID: AB_2904565 ), TGFβ2 (AbboMax Cat# 500–3784, RRID: AB_3086828 ) β-Tubulin (DSHB, Cat# AB_2315513; RRID: AB_528499 ). Validation of all used antibodies is available in the Reagent Validation File. Membranes were scanned to detect signal intensity using infrared imaging (Odyssey, LI-COR Biosciences) and quantified using ImageJ (NIH, USA).

A total of 15 embryos from three pregnant mice for each of the CON and MO groups at each of E9.5, E11.5 and E13.5 time points were collected for single-cell RNA sequencing. On the other hand, a total of five pregnant mice from each of the CON, MO, and MO-MET groups, as well as AMPK WT and AMPK KO groups were used to collect embryos at E13.5 for biochemical analysis. Each pregnancy was considered as an experimental unit. For cell culture studies, three separate experiments (n = 3) were carried out. Data were analysed using R version 4.3.1 and student's t-test or one-way ANOVA was used to compare statistical significance between or among groups. Data are reported as mean ± SEM and visualized using GraphPad Prism version 8.0.0 for Windows (GraphPad Software, Boston, Massachusetts, USA). Statistical differences were indicated as ∗ P < 0.05, ∗∗ P < 0.01, and ∗∗∗ P < 0.001.

All animal studies were conducted in AAALAC-approved facilities following ARRIVE guidelines 37 and approved by the Institute of Animal Care and Use Committees (IACUC) at the Washington State University (protocol number: 6704).

The funding sources did not play any role regarding the study's design, data acquisition, data analysis, interpretation, or report writing.
sections.results:
Fibroblasts are mesenchymal cells that originated from embryonic mesoderm along with myogenic, chondrogenic, osteogenic and adipogenic progenitor cells. 38 At E9.5, mesenchymal progenitor cells undergo lineage commitments and gradually migrate to their desired locations. Embryonic fibroblasts become distinguishable from other mesenchymal cells after E12.5. 39 To construct the single-cell transcriptomic profiles of mouse embryos, we collected embryos from C57BL/6J mice at three different embryonic days: E9.5, E11.5 and E13.5 ( Supplementary Fig. S1a ). After 10 weeks of HFD or control diet (CD), the MO group gained a 20% higher body weight than the CON group ( Supplementary Fig. S1b ). While the food intake was similar ( Supplementary Fig. S1c ), the HFD group had a higher fasting glucose level and lower glucose tolerance ( Supplementary Fig. S1d and e ). Embryos were collected at E9.5, E11.5, and E13.5 for scRNA-seq. A total of 75,402 cells were recovered by filtering out the low-quality cells ( Supplementary Fig. S1f ) for further analysis where 38,871 cells were from the CON group and 36,531 cells from the MO group with a median of 5458 genes and 32,822 unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) per cell.

We integrated all cells from three different time points: E9.5, E11.5 and E13.5 of both MO and CON groups together and performed unsupervised clustering using Seurat V4.3.0.1. We found 18 major distinct clusters ( Fig. 1 a) across the integrated dataset and determined the cell identities and cluster annotation based on the distribution of highly specific marker genes in each cluster ( Supplementary Fig. S2a , Supplementary Tables S1 and S2 ). For example, top marker genes for cluster 7: Myod1 and Myog are highly specific for myogenic cells; in cluster 4: Sox9 and Col2a1 are specific to chondroprogenitors and activated chondrogenic cells, 40 Gpc5 for embryonic mesenchymal cells (EMC) 34 and Myl2 and Myl4 are specific for cardiac muscle progenitor cells. On the other hand, the percentages of cells in major clusters showed progressive changes with the advances of embryonic days ( Supplementary Fig. S1g ). The first wave of myogenesis in murine embryos occurs during E10.5 to 12.5, 41 and in our integrated dataset, a gradual increase in the myogenic cell percentage from 0.70% (E9.5) to 6.21% (E13.5), showing active myogenesis. Similarly, a gradual increase was detected in the percentage of osteogenic cells in the osteochondrogenic cluster ( Supplementary Fig. S1g ). Importantly, there was difference in the number of cells between CON and MO groups in several major clusters including connective tissue progenitor (CT), early mesenchyme (EMS) and myogenic (MYO) clusters ( Fig. 1 b and c). Besides, MO impacted the gene expression in several major cell clusters ( Fig. 1 d). These data suggest the impact of MO on gene expression and cell lineage commitments during the embryonic development.

Single-cell transcriptomic profile of mouse embryos at embryonic days E9.5, 11.5 and 13.5 from Control (CON) and Maternal obes ity (MO) group . (a) Uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) plot showing 18 major clusters from integrated data sets from three different time points. Names of individual clusters are mentioned next to the figure along with their corresponding identification number. (b) UMAP showing clusters of cells from CON and MO groups. A major differential area between two groups is indicated by dotted circles. (c) Bar plots showing comparison between the numbers of each cell type in CON and MO groups. (d) Bar plot showing numbers of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) induced by MO in each cell type. Coral and Aqua bar indicates upregulated and downregulated DEGs respectively (obtained from edgeR, P < 0.05). (e) Representative enriched KEGG pathways of upregulated genes from integrated dataset due to MO. (f) Representative biological processes from Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) related to inflammatory response, transforming growth factor β (TGFβ) production, response to TGFβ and fibroblast proliferation enriched in upregulated genes due to MO. CON, Control group and MO, Maternal Obesity group. (See also Supplementary Tables S1, S2, and S4 ).

Transcriptomic profiles of different cell types were further analysed. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway analysis of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between CON and MO groups revealed a list of top enriched pathways ( Supplementary Tables S3–S6 ). KEGG pathways of “Extracellular matrix (ECM) receptor interaction” and GO terms “Extracellular matrix assembly” were enriched in the upregulated genes ( Fig. 1e and 2b and Supplementary Tables S3 and S4 ) in the MO group along with the “Acute inflammatory response”, “NF-κB signalling” and “IL-17 signalling pathway” ( Fig. 1 e, Supplementary Fig. S2b ). Gene set enrichment analysis suggested up-regulation of “Inflammatory response” ( Fig. 1 f) and “IL-1β production”, “IL-8 production”, “TNF production” and “cellular response to IFN-β” ( Supplementary Fig. S2c ). NF-κB is a key responder to inflammatory stimuli, 42 , 43 together with elevated expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1, IL-17 and TNFα, showing inflammatory response in MO embryos.

Identification of unique cell clusters with fibrogenic lineage cells and in vivo re-construction of the developmental trajectory from single-cell profiling in early mouse embryos . (a) Three major cell clusters identified by their top marker genes expression containing cells with fibrogenic lineages. (b) Distribution of fibroblast marker genes and other common extracellular matrix (ECM) synthesis genes in the fibrogenic lineage cell clusters. (c) Expression and density of fibroblast marker and ECM synthesis genes across three clusters of the fibrogenic lineage. (d) Monocle 3 trajectory plot of fibrogenic cell lineage. Figure on top right showing the location of each cluster in pseudo-time trajectory. Figures on bottom showing individual lineage tree projected of each of the EMC and EFA cluster to CT cluster. (e) Distribution of cells according to their types and according to their developmental stages (E9.5, E11.5, and E13.5) in the pseudo developmental trajectory. (f) Expression of fibroblast marker genes Pdgfra in fibrogenic cell lineage clusters with respect to pseudo-time coordinates. (g) Relative expression of Tgfb2 and Prrx1 in pseudo-time trajectory. (h) Relative expression of extracellular matrix synthesis genes in fibrogenic cell lineage clusters with respect to pseudo-time coordinates.

TGFβ is a pleiotropic anti-inflammatory cytokine involved in the differentiation and proliferation of wide varieties of cells. 44 Upregulated gene sets of “TGFβ production” and “Response to TGFβ” ( Fig. 1 f) suggest activation of anti-inflammatory response in MO during early embryonic development, consistent with the elevation of inflammation in MO embryos. Enrichment of multiple gene sets related to “Fibroblast proliferation”, “Fibroblast migration”, and “ECM assembly” ( Fig. 1 f, Supplementary Fig. S2c and e and Supplementary Tables S3 and S4 ) were identified in the upregulated genes and gene sets, while “Negative regulation of fibroblast proliferation” ( Supplementary Fig. S2d , Supplementary Table S5 ) was enriched among downregulated genes in MO embryos.

In summary, MO induced inflammatory response during early embryonic development accompanied with elevated TGFβ production which might increase the differentiation of multipotent EMCs into fibrogenic lineages.

Fibroblasts are distinct cell types critical for the synthesis of ECM proteins. 38 To explore the impact of MO on fibrogenic dynamics, fibrogenic lineage clusters were identified based on the expression patterns of marker genes: platelet-derived growth factor receptor-α ( Pdgfra ) and β ( Pdgfrb ). 38 We observed three cell clusters: CT, EMC, and embryonic fibro-adipogenic progenitor cells (EFA) expressing these marker genes at high levels, and computationally isolated for further exploration ( Fig. 2 a). Pdgfra , a known marker for mesenchymal cells and primary fibroblasts, 45 were distributed in all three major clusters ( Fig. 2 b and c).

We further characterized the clusters by the expression of common ECM marker genes Col1a1 , Col1a2, Col3a1 , Col5a2 and other genes distinct for each cluster ( Fig. 2 b and c and Supplementary Fig. S3a ). Cells in CT cluster were connective tissue progenitor cells that express the common ECM marker genes and distributed across the cluster ( Fig. 2 b and c and Supplementary Fig. S3a and c ). On the other hand, the EMC cluster belongs to early mesenchymal cells expressing mesenchyme specific genes, Gpc6, Hmga2, Peg3, Asb4 , and Lix1 ( Supplementary Fig. S3b and Supplementary Tables S1 and S2 ). 46 , 47 , 48 The EFA expressed pro-fibrogenic progenitor and tissue-specific fibrogenic marker genes, Foxd1, Meox1, Arg1 and Zic1 ( Supplementary Fig. S3b and Supplementary Tables S1 and S2 ). 49 , 50 , 51 , 52 Along with this, as the progenitor cells have both fibrogenic and adipogenic differentiation capabilities, we confirmed our identified clusters with common adipogenic marker genes: Zfp423, Cebpb and Pparg, which were also distributed in the UMAP of our isolated clusters ( Supplementary Fig. S3e and f ).

In summary, based on the single cell transcriptomes of early embryos, we identified distinct populations of early mesenchymal and fibrogenic progenitor cells, as well as more differentiated connective tissue progenitor cells. Altogether, they represent the primary populations of fibrogenic progenitor and more differentiated cells.

Next, we investigated how MO altered the developmental trajectories of fibrogenic cells during the early embryonic development. We computationally sorted all cells of the fibrogenic lineage in embryos at three time points ( Fig. 2 d) and used Monocle 3 to develop fibrogenesis-specific pseudo-developmental trajectory ( Fig. 2 e). We placed the progenitor cells of EMC and EFA clusters from E9.5, expressing the common ECM gene in a low extent, at the beginning of the clusters and highly ECM gene expressing cells of E13.5 at the trajectory terminal. The pseudo-development trajectory and expression of both Pdgfra ( Fig. 2 f) and Pdgfrb ( Supplementary Fig. S3c ) in pseudo-time points suggest upregulation during the differentiation of EMC and EFA progenitor cells into more committed and differentiated cells towards the CT cluster. We further calculated the expression of fibrogenic differentiation marker genes Col1a1 , Col1a2, Col3a1 , Col5a2, Col4a1, Col4a5, Col6a1 and Col6a2 ( Fig. 2 h and Supplementary Fig. S3d ), which code for collagens in ECM and followed a similar upregulated pattern as Pdgfra and Pdgfrb . To check the adipogenic potential of our isolated cluster in pseudo-time trajectory, we analysed common pre-adipocyte marker genes: Zfp423, Cebpb and Pparg ( Supplementary Fig. S3h ) . Zfp423 was identified in the committed adipogenic precursor cells and Pparg is required for terminal differentiation to adipocytes which activates after onset of CEBPB. 53 , 54 Pparg was not detected in the pseudo temporal trajectory ( Supplementary Fig. S3h ), suggesting adipogenic differentiation was not ongoing at this early stage.

TGFβ is the key factor stimulating fibroblast proliferation and fibrogenesis. 19 We explored the expression levels of all three TGF-β isoforms for their possible correlation with the progression of fibrogenesis. Across the pseudo developmental trajectory, Tgfb2 exhibited a continuous upregulation ( Fig. 2 g) whereas expression of other two isoforms Tgfb1 and Tgfb3 were not detected ( Supplementary Fig. S3g ). Prrx1 is a downstream response factor of TGFβ and a master transcription factor of fibroblast lineage determination. 20 , 55 Activated and migrating fibroblasts highly express Prrx1 , which binds to the super-enhancer of Col gene family members and enhances their expression. 55 The expression of Prrx1 was upregulated throughout the pseudo-time trajectory ( Fig. 2 h), which implies higher migration of fibrogenic cells during embryonic development in the MO group. 56

Taken together, these findings suggest an increasing expression of fibrogenic marker genes in the pseudo-time trajectory, which correlates with the upregulation of Tgfb and Prrx1 .

During early embryogenesis, mesenchymal progenitor cells originate from two major sources: mesoderm and neural crest, 57 which contribute to progressive and tissue-specific fibrosis under pathophysiological conditions. To analyse the impact of MO on the upregulation of embryonic fibrogenesis, we analysed the expression of common marker genes of fibrogenesis along with Tgfb throughout the three embryonic developmental time points E9.5, E11.5 and E13.5.

As shown in Fig. 3 a and b, there was a distinct difference in the cell populations between CON and MO groups in fibrogenic clusters. The percentage of cells in CT clusters increased to 29.9% in the MO group from 13.3% in the CON group (increased by ∼125%). Consistent with this finding, as the embryonic day progressed, the cell populations of the EMC and EFA clusters decreased at a rate greater in the MO group relative to the CON group whereas increased in CT cluster in MO (54.47%) compared with CON group (35.32%) ( Fig. 3 c).

Maternal obesity enhances the number of cells with fibrogenic potential in early mouse embryo . (a) Integrated UMAP of three fibrogenic clusters showing relative distribution of cells in CON and MO groups. (b) Relative percentages of cells and their distribution in the UMAP from each of the three fibrogenic lineage clusters from CON and MO groups in the integrated data set of E9.5, E11.5 and E13.5. Numbers on the top right corner of each UMAP denote the cell population for the respective cluster. (c) Relative percentages and distribution of cells belong to each fibrogenic lineage cell clusters in the UMAP during three embryonic time points E9.5–E13.5 in CON and MO groups. The number in the right corner of each UMAP denote the percentage of that specific cell types in whole embryo and the line graph below represents the pattern of changes in cell number with the progression of embryonic days. CON, Control group; MO, Maternal Obesity group.

MO induced differential gene expressions in fibrogenic clusters ( Fig. 4 a). The expression of EMC marker genes, Col1a1 , Col1a2, Col3a1, Col5a2, Col6a2, and Col6a3 was elevated due to MO ( Fig. 4 c, Supplementary Fig. S4a and Supplementary Table S7 ), as well as the marker gene of fibrogenic progenitor cells, Pdgfra ( Fig. 4 b). On the other hand, the expression level of Pdgfrb was very low across the fibrogenic clusters with no significant difference, suggesting its lower contribution in primary fibrogenesis ( Fig. 4 b). Consistently, the expression of adipocyte lineage markers Zfp423 , Adipoq and Cebpb did not elevate in MO ( Supplementary Fig. S4c , Supplementary Table S8 ).

Maternal obesity enhances the expression of fibrogenic and extracellular matrix (ECM) genes in early mouse embryo . (a) Volcano plot of differentially expressed genes in Maternal obesity (MO) group relative to control (CON) group in the fibrogenic cluster. Significance (adjusted P -value) was calculated in Seurat using the non-parametric Wilcoxon rank-sum test. (b) Violin plot showing relative expression of fibroblast marker genes Pdgfra and Pdgfrb in embryos from CON and MO groups in fibrogenic lineage clusters. (c) Violin plot showing relative expression of major extracellular matrix (ECM) synthesis genes, between CON and MO embryos. (d) Relative expression of Tgfb2 in CON and MO groups and in three different embryonic time points: E9.5, E11.5 and E13.5 fibrogenic lineage clusters. (e) Relative expression of Prrx1 embryos from CON and MO groups. (f) Adjust P -value of upregulated genes in MO group involved in TGFβ signalling and regulation of SMAD across all clusters. CON, Control group; MO, Maternal Obesity group. (See also Supplementary Table S7 and Supplementary Table S8 ).

MO induced an elevation of Tgfb2 and Prrx1 ( Fig. 4 d and e) but not the Tgfb1 and Tgfb3 ( Supplementary Fig. S4b ). The expression of Tgfb2 increased along with the progression of embryonic days from E9.5 to E13.5 ( Fig. 3 f), consistent with enhanced fibrogenic activity in MO shown in the pseudo developmental trajectory ( Fig. 2 g). TGFβ signalling pathway activates SMADs through phosphorylation. 58 MO upregulated the expression of genes ( Ppm1a, Hipk2, Ctdspl2, Pdcd4, Usp15, Usp9x) involved in the post-translational modification of SMAD ( Fig. 4 f). 29

In short, single-cell transcriptomic analysis suggested that MO substantially upregulates overall fibrogenesis during embryonic development, accompanied with the activation of TGFβ/PRRX1 pathway in fibrogenic clusters.

To quantify the intracellular communication network among the cell clusters, we used CellChat in a label-base mode. 59 Cell to cell communication analysis of integrated datasets from E9.5 to E13.5 revealed a strong communication of progenitor cell clusters EMC and EFA with the differentiated cell clusters: MYO, OC, and CT ( Fig. 5 a), and comparative analysis of CON and MO datasets identified multiple differential interactions between two groups ( Fig. 5 b and Supplementary Fig. S5a ). The BMP, non-canonical WNT, TGFβ, IGF and FGF were identified as major incoming and outgoing signalling pathways in the early embryos ( Fig. 5 c and Supplementary Fig. S5b ). Comparative analysis of major signalling pathways between CON and MO groups reveals elevated incoming TGFβ signalling of the fibrogenic lineage cell clusters: CT, EMC and EFA ( Fig. 5 d), and EMC and EFA were strong receivers of TGFβ signalling in MO ( Fig. 5 e). Notably, ligand-receptor (L-R) interaction analysis identified that TGFβ2 was the dominant ligand and their multimeric TGFβR1/TGFβR2 receptors were dominated in the embryonic TGFβ signalling of all clusters ( Fig. 4 f) and in fibrogenic lineage clusters ( Supplementary Fig. S5c ). L-R interaction analysis of fibrogenic lineage also revealed that CT, EMC and EFA in MO groups responded to TGFβ as evident by elevated expression of Tgfbr1 and Tgfbr2 receptors ( Fig. 5 g).

Maternal Obesity induces differential cell to cell communication and enhances Ligand-Receptor (L-R) activity of TGFβ signalling pathway in early embryos . (a) Cell–cell communication networks identify significant communications across all cell clusters. (b) Circle plot showing the number of differential interactions among three fibrogenic cell lineage clusters and other clusters due to MO. (c) Incoming signalling pathways in all cell clusters in the integrated dataset from embryonic time points E9.5, E11.5 and E13.5. Red box showing overall TGFβ activity. (d) Heatmap showing comparison of major signalling pathways between CON and MO groups. (e) Heatmap showing the differential role of TGFβ signalling pathways between CON and MO groups. (f) Bar chart showing contribution of each Ligand-Receptor pair involved in TGFβ signalling. (g) Receptors expression involved in TGFβ signalling pathways between CON and MO groups. CON, Control group; MO, Maternal Obesity group.

To conclude, these data showed that MO alters the cell-to-cell communication between fibrogenic linage clusters, evidenced by the greater activity of TGFβ signal receivers and targets in the MO group.

To further verify the elevated fibrogenic activity identified through scRNA-seq, we examined the expression of key fibrogenic progenitor marker genes Pdgfra , and Tgfb2 as well as highly expressed common ECM genes identified from scRNA-seq, Col1a1, Col1a2, Col3a1, Col5a2, and Prrx1 in E13.5 embryos. Consistently, the mRNA expression levels of Pdgfra , ECM genes, as well as Prrx1 were elevated in MO embryos ( Fig. 6 a). However, fibrogenic marker gene Pdgfrb ( Supplementary Fig. S6a ) and the adipogenic marker genes Zfp423 and Adipoq did not exhibit elevation in MO ( Supplementary Fig. S6a ).

MO enhances fibrogenesis via upregulation of PRRX1 and inhibition of AMPK in embryos at E 13.5 . (a) Relative mRNA expression of fibroblast marker genes Pdgfra and Tgfb2 , and common ECM synthesis genes Col1a1, Col3a1, Col5a2 and Col6a3 , and Prrx1 in CON (n = 5 mice per group) and MO (n = 5 mice per group) groups. (b) Cropped Western Blots of pP65, P65, pSMAD3, SMAD3, and PRRX1 (β-Tubulin as loading control) from CON (n = 5 maternal mice per group) and MO (n = 5 maternal mice per group) embryos. (c) Cropped Western Blots of pAMPK, AMPK and TGFβ2 (β-Tubulin as loading control) from CON (n = 5 maternal mice per group) and MO (n = 5 maternal mice per group) embryos. (d) Breeding of PDGFRα EGFP male mice with CON and MO female mice. (e) In vivo fluorescence image and measurement of fluorescence signal from CON and MO embryos at E13.5. (f) Sections (Left: paraxial mesoderm; right: adjacent area) from E13.5 CON and MO embryos visualizing PDGFRα+ fibrogenic cells distribution. CON: Control group; MO: Maternal Obesity group. Data are shown as mean ± SEM, and each dot represents one litter. ∗ P < 0.05, ∗∗ P < 0.01, and ∗∗∗ P < 0.001 in CON versus MO by one-tailed unpaired Student's t test (a–e).

Inflammation induces TGFβ signalling which enhances the synthesis and accumulation of ECM proteins. 60 , 61 To verify, we further analysed the alteration in NF-κB signalling due to MO. Indeed, the protein level of pP65, the key mediator of canonical NF-κB signalling, was enhanced by MO ( Fig. 6 b, Supplementary Fig. S6b ). Importantly, the increased pSMAD3/SMAD3 ratio, a key mediator of TGFβ signalling along with elevated PRRX1 and TGFβ2 levels ( Fig. 6 b and c; Supplementary Fig. S6b ), showed an overall enhancement of TGFβ/PRRX1 signalling activity in MO embryos. Furthermore, phosphorylation of Thr-172 is required for the activation of AMPK, and we found that the pAMPK level and pAMPK/AMPK ratio were lower in MO embryos ( Fig. 6 c, Supplementary Fig. S6c ), consistent with previous reports that MO inhibits AMPK activity in fetal tissues. 26 , 27

To visualize the activity and distribution of fibrogenic progenitors, we conducted lineage tracing of PDGFRα+ cells in both CON and MO embryos. In vivo fluorescence imaging of embryos at E13.5 confirmed higher fluorescence signal in the MO group ( Fig. 6 e). Along with this, cryosections of MO E13.5 embryos exhibited a higher number of PDGFRα+ cells ( Fig. 6 f).

Collectively, in line with the up-regulation of fibrogenesis observed in scRNA-seq data, biochemical analyses showed that MO inhibits AMPK while promoting the TGFβ/PRRX1 pathway and elevating the number of fibrogenic progenitor cells and overall fibrogenesis.

C3H/10T1/2 cells are multipotent mesenchymal progenitor cells derived from mouse embryos, with the capacity to differentiate into various cell lineages, including osteoblasts, chondrocytes, adipocytes, and muscle cells. 62 The fibrogenic differentiation of C3H/10T1/2 cells can be induced by TGFβ stimulation. 58 Metformin and A769662 are well known activators of AMPK; to explore the potential mediating role of AMPK in fibrogenesis, we exposed C3H/10T1/2 cells to TGFβ for 48 h in the presence metformin or A769662. 63 , 64 The treatment with TGFβ increased the mRNA expression of fibrogenic markers, including Col1a1 , Col1a2 , Col3a1 , Col5a2 , and Prrx1 . Notably, AMPK activation inhibited TGFβ-induced elevation of fibrogenic markers ( Fig. 7 a).

Activation of AMPK suppresses fibrogenesis through inhibiting TGFβ signalling and Prrx1 expression. (d) Sirius red staining of collagen (visualized by red) in C3H/10T1/2 cells after incubation with 10 ng/ml TGFβ in the presence and absence of 500 μM AMPK activator MET (Metformin) and 50 μM of A76 (A769662) for 96 h. Scale bars, 400 μM. Data are presented as mean ± SEM, and each dot represents one independent experiment. ∗ P < 0.05, ∗∗ P < 0.01, and ∗∗∗ P < 0.001 groups by one-way ANOVA (n = 3). (e) AMPK activation in MO mice by metformin (f) Relative mRNA expression of fibroblast marker genes Pdgfra, Prrx1, and Tgfb2, and common ECM synthesis genes Col1a1, Col1a2, Col3a1 and Col5a2 and (g) Cropped WB image showing protein content of pAMPK, AMPK, COL1A1, TGFβ2 and PRRX1 from CON (n = 5 maternal mice per group), MO (n = 5 maternal mice per group), and MO-MET (n = 5 maternal mice per group) embryos after treatment with metformin during pregnancy. β-Tubulin was used as loading control (Loading control used for COL1A1, TGFβ2 and PRRX1 was also used as loading control for Supplementary Fig. S7d ). Data are presented as mean ± SEM, and each dot represents one litter. ∗ P < 0.05, ∗∗ P < 0.01, and ∗∗∗ P < 0.001 groups by one-way ANOVA (n = 5).

At the protein level, the addition of AMPK activators elevated the pAMPK/AMPK ratio and reduced the contents of phosphorylated SMAD3 and PRRX1 ( Fig. 7 b). Picrosirius red staining further demonstrated an enhancement in ECM synthesis due to TGFβ, which was effectively inhibited by metformin and A769662 ( Fig. 7 c). Remarkably, the addition of TGFβ increased cell density, indicating enhanced fibroblast proliferation, 65 which was attenuated by AMPK activation ( Supplementary Fig. S7a ).

To further verify in vivo , we treated obese mice with 0.2% metformin via drinking water during pregnancy ( Fig. 7 e, Supplementary Fig. S7b and c ) and collected the embryos at E13.5. Metformin robustly activated AMPK in embryos ( Fig. 7 g). Metformin also reduced the expression of fibrogenic marker genes Pdgfra and Prrx1 , as well as the expression of Tgfb 2 and members of collagen synthesis gene family: Col1a1 , Col1a2 , Col3a1 , Col5a2 . Western blot analysis showed that metformin reduced COL1a1 synthesis along with TGFβ2 and PRRX1 levels in MO embryos ( Fig. 7 g). Consistently, the inflammatory marker pP65/P65 ratio was reduced ( Supplementary Fig. S7d ).

In summary, AMPK activation inhibited the TGFβ/SMAD signalling pathway and collagen synthesis induced by TGFβ both in vivo and in vitro suggesting metformin as a therapeutic agent for the intervention of elevated embryonic fibrogenesis due to MO.

Considering that AMPK activators might exert nonspecific effects, we further analysed the mediatory roles of AMPK in embryonic fibrogenesis using mesenchymal cells separated from AMPK WT and inducible KO mice ( Fig. 8 a). Because AMPKα1 (Gene name: Prkaa1 ) is mainly expressed in progenitor cells, AMPKα1 knockout (AMPK KO) dramatically reduces, but does not abolish AMPK activity, due to the compensatory AMPKα2 expression, which mimicks AMPK suppression due to MO. 9 Following AMPK KO by 4-hydroxytamoxifen, the expression of , Col1a1 and Col3a1, as well as Pdgfra and Prrx1 were elevated, together with higher collagen accumulation in AMPK KO cells ( Fig. 8 b). AMPK KO significantly reduced the AMPKα level but increased the ratio of pSMAD3/SMAD3 and PRRX1 content ( Fig. 8 c). Furthermore, Picrosirius red staining showed enhanced ECM synthesis in AMPK KO cells ( Supplementary Fig. S8a ). AMPKα1 KO reduced cell proliferation, 66 but increased after the induction of fibrosis by TGFβ ( Supplementary Fig. S8b ). These data show that AMPK inhibition due to AMPKα1 KO promotes fibrogenesis in primary cultured embryonic mouse cells.

To verify in vivo , we produced E13.5 AMPKα1 deficient embryos by breeding to produce AMPKα1 fl/fl -CreER (AMPK KO) and AMPKα1 fl/fl (AMPK-WT) embryos, which were injected with tamoxifen ( Fig. 8 d and e; Supplementary Fig. S8c and S8d ). As expected, Pdgfrα and Prrx1 were upregulated in AMPK deficient embryos ( Fig. 8 f and g). Consistently, the expression of members of Col gene family and synthesis of collagen were elevated in AMPK-KO embryos in comparison with AMPK-WT embryos ( Fig. 8 f and g).

Taken together, AMPK is essential to regulate the fibrogenesis in embryos, and AMPK deficiency robustly increased the fibrogenic activity during the early embryonic development in response to MO.
sections.discussion:
Regardless of ethnicity, age, or parity, the prevalence of pre-pregnancy obesity among women has increased at an alarming rate over the past decades. 67 The negative effects of MO on the development and function of major organs of offspring have been well documented, 3 , 68 of prominence the enhanced fibrosis in multiple tissues and organs of MO offspring. 5 , 7 , 9 , 10 , 12 , 13 , 14 , 15 In this study, we delineated the single-cell transcriptomic profiles of mouse embryos impacted by MO, demonstrating that MO profoundly elevates fibrogenic activity in embryos, showing an embryonic origin of fibrosis in MO offspring.

During embryogenesis, primary fibroblasts in the mesoderm give rise to fibrogenic progenitor cells which progressively differentiate into fibroblasts and myofibroblasts in adult tissues. 69 While tissue resident fibroblasts are largely quiescent, they are activated under fibrotic stimuli, 38 contributing to extracellular matrix synthesis, tissue damage repair and fibrosis. 38 The differentiation and activation of these progenitor cells into activated fibroblasts was primarily instigated by factors such as TGFβ, connective tissue growth factor (CTGF), and various signalling molecules. 70 Accompanied with inflammation, our study revealed an elevation of Tgfb in MO embryos in response to inflammatory activity. 19 Among the three isoforms of TGFβ, TGFβ1 is ubiquitously expressed, but notably, we found an elevation of TGFβ2 during the early embryonic stage. In agreement, TGFβ2 is required for optimal development and cell fate determination during embryogenesis 71 , 72 ; therefore, upregulated TGFβ2 signalling promotes the proliferation of fibrogenic progenitor cells as well as directs their differentiation into fibroblasts and subsequent activation. 38 The gradual increase in the more differentiated connective tissue progenitor cells, and the subsequent decrease in early mesenchymal cells and fibrogenic progenitor cells in MO embryos suggest the impact of TGFβ upsurge in priming the progenitor cell fates to a fibrogenic differentiation. In addition, we identified an upregulation of Prrx1 in both transcriptomic profile and in cultured cells. PRRX1 in activated fibroblasts enhances the TGFβ signalling by forming complex with SMAD3, a key mediator of TGFβ signalling pathway. 55

AMPK serves as a pivotal regulator of cellular metabolism, activated due to cellular stress or negative energy balance. 9 , 27 , 73 It phosphorylates key molecules of multiple metabolic pathways which increases catabolism to restore energy balance. Notably, we found a pronounced inhibition of AMPK phosphorylation in MO embryos, concomitant with an elevation in the phosphorylation of SMAD3 as well as an upsurge in TGFβ signalling. 5 , 7 , 9 To test the regulatory role of AMPK in embryonic fibrogenesis, we used pharmacological activation of AMPK by metformin and A769660, as well as transgenic mice. AMPK activation inhibited TGFβ signalling and Prrx1 expression, while AMPKα1 knockout in isolated embryonic fibroblasts elevated TGFβ signalling and Prrx1 expression, confirming the effect of AMPK in ameliorating fibrogenesis in embryos. In agreement, organ-specific activation of AMPK in liver, lung, or adipocytes by metformin or other methods decreased fibrogenic activity. 23 , 24 , 74 AMPK is a common drug target for treating type 2 diabetics and associated metabolic disorders. 75

Metformin, a known activator of AMPK, is used by women with polycystic ovarian syndrome, severe obesity, and gestational diabetes. 76 , 77 Metformin can effectively cross placenta into the fetal circulation. 78 Despite the fibrogenic inhibitory effects found in our study, in a previous mouse study, embryos exposed to metformin treatment during the entire gestational period exhibited higher body weight during their adult age in a sex specific manner. 79 Similarly, metformin treatment during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy led to lower birth weight, larger upper-arm circumferences and bicep skinfold thickness, increased subcutaneous fat deposition though not the overall body fat in offspring. 80 On the other hand, in other studies, metformin treatment during the first trimester of pregnancy did not induce developmental anomalies and adverse effects on fetal development. 81 , 82 Since unplanned pregnancy accounts for ∼40% of all pregnancies and most women usually discover pregnancy after 5–6 weeks (equivalent to E12.5–13.5 in mice), a substantial number of early embryos are exposed to metformin and more information is needed to better comprehend the impacts of metformin on early embryonic development. 83 , 84 One major implication of our findings is that metformin treatment during early pregnancy suppresses TGFβ/PRRX1 pathway and fibrosis in embryonic cells through activation of AMPK, suggesting it as an effective therapeutic agent for reducing inflammation and embryonic fibrosis caused by MO.

In this study, based on scRNA-seq data, we did not find cellular difference between embryo sexes. This might be due to the early stage of embryos which were before sexual differentiation. Therefore, for remaining analyses, we did not separate embryos based on sex. Another limitation is the use of whole embryos for scRNA-seq. Due to the lack of known differences in fibrogenic differentiation among tissues and organs, we were not able to separate fibrogenesis based on specific tissues or organs. For these analyses, individual organs and tissues need to be separated first and then sequenced separately, which warrants further studies.

In summary, our single-cell transcriptomic profiling of mouse embryos revealed that MO induces low-grade inflammatoion and profoundly upregulates embryonic fibrogenesis, which was associated with AMPK inhibition. AMPK activation downregulates TGFβ-induced collagen synthesis and fibrogenesis. Thus, pharmaceutical activation of AMPK by drugs such as metformin may ameliorate embryonic fibrogenesis due to MO. In addition, our data emphasize the critical changes of cell lineage commitments of early embryos due to MO, which occur earlier than most women discover pregnancy. These data undescore the importance of early intervention in improving the health of children born to mothers with obesity.
